name: Nevada

notes: Food for home consumption is exempt.
Alcohol is taxed at the general rate, on top of per-gallon excise taxes left out here (liquor over 22% $3.60, 14% to 22% $1.30, up to 14% 70 cents, beer 16 cents).

Cigarettes and other tobacco are taxed at the general rate, on top of excise taxes left out here ($1.80 a pack of cigarettes; other tobacco by its wholesale price, premium cigars at most 50 cents each).
Household supplies: diapers (for children and adults) are exempt from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2050 (2024 Question 5), which is not taken out here.
Personal care products: feminine hygiene products are exempt from January 1, 2019 to December 31, 2028 (2018 Question 2), which is not taken out here.
Barber and beauty services, laundry and dry cleaning, and auto repair labor: not taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).

Motor fuel is exempt from the sales tax and pays per-gallon taxes instead: 33 cents in most counties (23 cents state, 9 cents county option and 1 cent), 28 cents in Esmeralda, Eureka, Lincoln and Storey counties, and more in Clark and Washoe counties, which index theirs (about 62.75 cents in all in Clark in fiscal 2027); left out here.

Hotel stays pay the sales tax plus county and city room taxes (in unincorporated Clark County, where the Strip is: 13.38% in the primary gaming corridor, 13% elsewhere in the school district area, 12.5% outside it and 10.5% more than 35 miles out, by Clark County tables; 13% in the city of Las Vegas, as reported; 13% or 13.5% in Reno and Sparks plus a nightly surcharge downtown; 11% in Carson City); not counted here.
Admission to live entertainment at venues holding 200 or more pays a 9% live entertainment tax instead; not counted here.

Nevada has no sales tax holiday for the general public; Nevada National Guard members and their families can claim a refund of the sales tax on purchases made October 30 to November 1, 2026 (Department of Taxation), not reflected here.
gaps: Nevada's 6.85% statewide rate is used as the state rate, following the state's own description of it, but only 2% of it goes to the State General Fund: 2.6% is the Local School Support Tax and 2.25% the city-county relief taxes. County add-ons in 13 of the 17 counties (to 7.1%-8.375%) are local; every county's rate matches the Department of Taxation's return form (REV-F013A, version 2025.1).
Nevada has no city sales taxes. The tourism improvement districts (NRS 271A) in the rate files charge their county's rate; they keep a share of the sales tax collected inside them instead.

local: Las Vegas – Symphony Park Tourism Improvement District
Reno – Freight House Tourism Improvement District
excludes the existing retail and Bully's on the National Bowling Stadium's first floor

programs: Redevelopment areas are mapped for Las Vegas (Redevelopment Areas 1, 2 and 3; Area 1 runs to 2046 after its extension), Reno (Redevelopment Districts 1 and 2), Carson City, Elko, Douglas County and Henderson (its five: Cornerstone, Downtown, Eastside, Lakemoor Canyon and Tuscany, from the city's open-data layer, 2019), and Reno's downtown business improvement district. North Las Vegas', Mesquite's, Sparks' and Boulder City's have no published maps and aren't shown. Tourism improvement districts (NRS 271A) keep a share of the sales tax collected inside them but charge the county's rate: Las Vegas' Symphony Park district and Reno's Cabela's, Freight House and Tessera districts are mapped from the cities' layers; the others (among them Las Vegas' Casino Center, South Rancho Drive and Tropicana districts and Sparks') have no published maps. Nevada Main Street's programs (among them Boulder City, Henderson, Las Vegas, Mesquite, Reno, Sparks, Ely, Tonopah and Virginia City) have no map.

warn.text: Amargosa Valley's page is built from a census tract it shares with Beatty; that tract's flag as a visitor economy draws on 9 lodging places (4.1 per 1,000 residents), mostly Beatty's motels near Death Valley, so read that flag with care.

Battle Mountain may carry the visitor caution only because of its motels along Interstate 80 (6 lodging places, 3.0 per 1,000 residents), serving travelers and mine workers rather than tourists, so read that caution with care.

Carlin may carry the visitor caution only because of its motels along Interstate 80 (5 lodging places, 2.4 per 1,000 residents), serving travelers and mine workers rather than tourists, so read that caution with care.

Hawthorne may carry the visitor caution only because of its motels on US 95 (7 lodging places, 2.4 per 1,000 residents), serving travelers and the Army depot more than tourists, so read that caution with care.

Las Vegas draws many visitors (downtown casinos and Fremont Street), but it isn't flagged as a visitor economy over the city as a whole: {visitor_why}. Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local.

McGill's page is built from a census tract it shares with Baker; that tract's visitor caution draws on 5 lodging places (3.4 per 1,000 residents) near Great Basin National Park, not in McGill, so read that caution with care.

Reno draws many visitors (its casinos and nearby Lake Tahoe), but it isn't flagged as a visitor economy over the city as a whole: {visitor_why}. Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local.
Wells' flag as a visitor economy draws on its motels along Interstate 80 (12 lodging places, 5.1 per 1,000 residents), serving travelers passing through, so read that flag with care.
